question.text: A transmitting antenna has a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>320</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and that of receiving antenna is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The maximum distance between them for satisfactory communication in line of sight mode is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math>. The value of  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> is ________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
Recall the formula of maximum distance between transmitting antenna and receiving antenna for satisfactory communication in terms of the radius of the earth and height of antennas, 

d=2Rh1+2Rh2⇒d=2×6400×0.32+2×6400×2≈224 km
